Dạng robot/use case: Sheet-metal cover panel bend design for a robot enclosure
Geometry/feature: Bent flange, inside bend radius, door/cover panel with mounting-flange height
Material grade: Aluminum 6061 (bend radius increased to 1.5t or larger to prevent grain cracking) or steel; 12-gauge minimum recommended for doors larger than ~600x800mm
Welding requirement: None (formed, not welded, for this feature)

Critical tolerance: Precision-tier: linear +/-0.20 mm, hole diameter +/-0.08 mm, bend angle +/-0.5 degree

Critical characteristic: Bend-radius-to-thickness ratio and die selection directly determine whether a designed flange/mounting-pattern geometry is actually achievable

Tooling/NRE need: Bend die selection changes with plate thickness (wider die needed for thicker plate), which can conflict with existing flange/hole-pattern designs
Raw claim/fact: Sheet-metal enclosure design guidance: inside bend radius should be roughly 1x material thickness for most steels, increased to 1.5t or more for 6061 aluminum to prevent grain cracking; standard laser-cut+bent tolerances hold linear dimensions to +/-0.45mm and holes to +/-0.12mm (tightening to +/-0.20mm/+/-0.08mm on precision work), with minimum flange height = 2x thickness + inside bend radius; 12-gauge is recommended as the practical minimum for enclosure doors larger than about 600x800mm.
